description: The scaffolding that wraps every book: a caregiver-coaching page, a pre-reading warm-up, a tricky-word list, a comprehension-prompt bank, and the cumulative-review rule. Most fields are auto-derivable from reading-levels.json, gpc-table.json, heart-words.json, and the book's four_questions.

caregiver_page.purpose: One page (front or back matter) that turns a parent into an effective coach in 30 seconds.

fields.sounds_practiced: New GPCs at this level (from gpc-table.json where level == book level).
fields.heart_words_previewed: Heart words introduced at this level (from heart-words.json).
fields.tricky_words_to_preview: Any out-of-level personalization/theme tokens used in this book (from book-spec.allowed_tokens).

do: Slide through the sounds slowly, then say it fast.
Cover part of the word and read the first chunk, then the rest.
Find a sound you know inside the word.
You said it — now reread the whole sentence so it flows.
avoid: Look at the picture to figure out the word.
What word would make sense there?
coaching_prompts.why: The 'do' prompts point the child back to decoding (the reliable strategy). The 'avoid' prompts are three-cueing habits that undercut decoding. Pictures are for meaning and confirmation, not word identification.

pre_reading_warm_up.purpose: A 60-second warm-up before reading, all done aloud/with sound cards.

steps.content: Say the new GPC sounds for this level, then a few from prior levels (cumulative).
Blend 3-4 decodable words that appear in the book (e.g., s-a-m -> Sam).
Read the level's heart words, marking the 'by heart' part.
Say and point to any out-of-level tokens (name, theme word) once, so they are not a surprise.

comprehension_bank.purpose: Post-reading prompts tied to the comprehension strand of skills-matrix.json and the book's four_questions. Ask 2-3, matched to the book level.

prompts: What did {who} try before it worked?
What would happen if they had given up?
How did {who} feel, and how do you know?

cumulative_review_rule.statement: Every book must revisit previously-taught patterns, not only the level's new focus. Target: at least 40% of decodable running words use GPCs from BELOW the current level, so practice is distributed and spaced across the child's whole sequence.
cumulative_review_rule.rationale: Distributed, cumulative review is core to structured literacy; it prevents 'learn it Tuesday, forget it Friday.'

sounds_practiced: review: short a, short i, short o
